Case_09003/figure7.jpg.source_caption: Growth from anaerobic bottle on blood agar plate.

description.short_caption: Growth on blood agar plate from anaerobic culture.
description.detailed_description: The image shows a blood agar plate with visible bacterial growth. The colonies appear as small, round, and slightly raised formations, with some areas showing hemolysis (clearing of the red agar). The plate is being held by a gloved hand, suggesting sterile handling. The growth is consistent with an organism cultured under anaerobic conditions.

description.short_caption: Coronal CT showing tubular abnormality in the abdomen (arrows).

The image is de-identified and does not include patient information.

description.short_caption: Abdominal radiograph showing gas patterns and bowel loops.
description.detailed_description: This is an abdominal radiograph in an anteroposterior (AP) view. The image shows the abdominal cavity with visible gas patterns and bowel loops. There is no clear evidence of free air under the diaphragm or other acute abnormalities. The bony structures, including the pelvis and lower ribs, are visible. The soft tissue outlines are also discernible.

description.short_caption: Gram stain showing thin, gram-negative rods.
description.detailed_description: This image shows a Gram stain with numerous thin, pink-staining (gram-negative) rods scattered across the field. The rods are uniform in size and shape, with some clustering visible. The background is clear, and there are no other cell types or debris evident. The staining technique highlights the gram-negative nature of the bacteria.

description.short_caption: Coronal CT scan of the abdomen and pelvis showing abnormal gas and fluid collections.
description.detailed_description: This coronal CT image of the abdomen and pelvis demonstrates abnormal findings, including prominent gas-filled loops of bowel and fluid collections. There is evidence of distension and possible bowel wall thickening. The image also shows a large, well-defined hyperdense area in the upper abdomen, suggestive of a fluid or abscess collection. Surrounding structures appear displaced, and there may be signs of inflammation or infection.
visible_findings: large hyperdense area in the upper abdomen
